answer: Picture honest agents as a crowded terrace of neighbors who vouch for each other through many small, repeated trades. A sybil farm can mint thousands of fake identities, but they all reach the real network across a narrow bridge of a few genuine ties. Trust scoring that caps how much reputation can flow over any single bridge, like one lantern lighting only a short path, keeps the farm's weight near that of its few real links, however many accounts it spawns.
